title: Java: which APIs and framework defaults turn into vulnerabilities?
short: Never let outside data name the class it becomes, keep input out of queries and expressions, and move off Spring Boot 3.5, without free fixes since June 2026.
answer: Before your next release, move to JDK 25 or 21 and Spring Boot 4.1[^sbsupport], stop deserializing outside data into classes it names, and make Find Security Bugs or CodeQL a required check. Judge everything else by whether outside data can pick a class, become SQL, an expression or a command line, reach an XML parser, a path or a URL, or slip past an authorization rule.
audience: Developers and tech leads writing production Java, including Spring Boot services, and the security people who review it

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Run a supported JDK and Spring Boot, and patch every quarter.
items.text: OpenJDK ships fixes on the third Tuesday of January, April, July and October[^ojvuln]; October's fixed 48 CVEs[^oj1020]. Spring Boot 3.5 lost free fixes in June 2026 and 4.0 loses them in December; 4.1 keeps them until July 2027[^sbsupport]. Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines.

items.title: Never let outside data name the class it becomes.
items.text: Java deserialization creates whatever classes the stream names, and no filter runs unless you set one[^serfilter]. Jackson's default typing hands the same choice to the JSON[^jackson]. Read outside data as JSON into records or concrete DTOs.

items.title: Keep input out of queries, expressions and commands.
items.text: Bind JDBC and JPQL values as parameters, never parse SpEL or OGNL built from input, and start processes with a `ProcessBuilder` argument list. SQL injection, OS command injection and code injection rank 2nd, 9th and 10th in the 2025 CWE Top 25[^cwe].

items.title: Deny by default and keep management endpoints private.
items.text: Spring Security applies the first rule that matches[^ssauthz], so end with `.anyRequest().denyAll()` or `.authenticated()`. Expose only `health`, Boot's default[^actuator]: ActiveMQ's Jolokia endpoint let logged-in users run code (CVE-2026-34197), and CISA lists it as exploited[^amq][^kev].

items.title: Make the analyzers a required check.
items.text: Run Find Security Bugs on SpotBugs or CodeQL on every pull request[^fsb][^cql], and set Dependency-Check's `failBuildOnCVSS`: its default of 11 never fails the build[^odc].

items.title: Where does outside data enter?
items.text: Find the controllers, message listeners, uploads and batch jobs it touches. Each should bind a record or DTO made for that request, as Spring advises[^modelattr], not a JPA entity.

items.title: Who may call it, on which record?
items.text: Ask why for each new `permitAll()` and for any matcher placed after a broader one, since the first match wins[^ssauthz]. Missing authorization ranks 4th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]: check who owns the record, not just the login.

items.title: Can data choose a class or code?
Does it reach SQL, a process, XML, a path or a URL?
items.text: Check `createQuery` and `@Query` strings built with `+`, `ProcessBuilder`, new XML parser factories, `resolve(` and HTTP clients given URLs from input.

items.title: What does it expose?
items.text: Check `exposure.include`, new `SecurityFilterChain` beans, which turn off Boot's own actuator rules[^actuator], error details and logged secrets.

blocks.title: Java traps and what to use instead
items: **`ObjectInputStream.readObject()` and `XMLDecoder`.** The stream decides which classes are created, and gadget classes on the classpath turn that into code execution[^serfilter]. Tomcat's CVE-2025-24813 reached it through uploads and file-based session storage[^tomcat], and OWASP lists `XMLDecoder` as unsafe for untrusted input[^owaspdeser]. Where you must read Java serialization, set `jdk.serialFilter` to an allowlist ending in `!*`, with `maxbytes` and `maxdepth` limits[^serpattern].

**`activateDefaultTyping()` and `@JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.CLASS)`.** The JSON then names the class, and Jackson warns that the validator you pass is critical for security[^jackson]. Use `Id.NAME` and list the allowed subtypes[^fsb]. XStream with a relaxed allowlist, SnakeYAML without `SafeConstructor` and fastjson without safe mode have the same problem[^owaspdeser].

**`DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()` with its defaults.** JDK XML parsers fetch external DTDs and entities unless you turn on secure processing explicitly[^jaxp], and GeoServer's XXE (CVE-2025-58360) is on CISA's exploited list[^kev]. On JDK 22 and later, set `-Djdk.xml.dtd.support=deny`[^javaxml]; on older JDKs set `disallow-doctype-decl` on DOM and SAX factories and `SUPPORT_DTD` to false on StAX[^jaxp].

**`"WHERE id = " + id` in JDBC, JPQL or a native `@Query`.** Hibernate queries are injectable when you concatenate[^owaspsqli]. Bind `?` or `:name` parameters, and map sort columns and directions from a fixed list, since parameters can't stand for column names[^owaspsqli]. Spring Data JPA's `Sort` check on native queries could be bypassed until August (CVE-2026-47834)[^jpasort].

**`parseExpression(input)` in SpEL, and OGNL or templates built from input.** Spring says `StandardEvaluationContext` must never evaluate untrusted expressions and `SimpleEvaluationContext` restricts them only on a best-effort basis[^spel]. SpEL injection in Spring Cloud Function and OGNL injection in Confluence are on CISA's exploited list[^kev]. Pass input as variables to fixed expressions.

**`Class.forName(name)` and JNDI `lookup(name)` with names from data.** PaperCut's exploited CVE-2026-82078 let attackers who could change configuration run classpath code through unsafe reflection[^kev], and Log4Shell let anyone who controlled a log message run code loaded from LDAP[^log4j]. Map names from a fixed list.

**`@ModelAttribute` binding onto entities.** Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965) was remote code execution through data binding[^kev]. Spring recommends an object made for web binding or constructor binding, and `allowedFields` where you must bind properties[^modelattr]. Bind requests to records.

**`Runtime.exec(String)` and `sh -c`.** `exec(String)` splits the command on whitespace and is deprecated since JDK 18[^runtime]. Use `ProcessBuilder` with a fixed program and one list element per argument, put `--` before values that may start with a dash, and never pass input to `sh -c` or `cmd /c`.

**`base.resolve(name)`.** An absolute `name` replaces `base`, and `normalize()` drops `..` without checking symlinks[^path]. Require the normalized result to `startsWith(base)`, which compares whole name elements, and use `toRealPath()` where links matter[^path]. Check `ZipEntry` names the same way.

**`new URL(input).openStream()` and HTTP clients given URLs from input.** URL connections also open `file:` URLs[^fsb], and server-side request forgery ranks 22nd in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Allowlist hosts, check the resolved address and keep `HttpClient`'s default of not following redirects[^httpclient].

blocks.title: Tools that catch it
items: **Find Security Bugs.** Add `findsecbugs-plugin` to the SpotBugs Maven or Gradle plugin and fix `OBJECT_DESERIALIZATION`, `JACKSON_UNSAFE_DESERIALIZATION`, `XXE_DOCUMENT`, `SQL_INJECTION_JPA`, `SPEL_INJECTION` and `COMMAND_INJECTION` first[^fsb].
**Error Prone.** `BanJNDI` is an error by default; turn on the experimental `BanSerializableRead` and `BanClassLoader` checks[^ep].
**CodeQL.** `java/unsafe-deserialization`, `java/xxe`, `java/spel-expression-injection`, `java/jndi-injection`, `java/zipslip` and `java/spring-boot-exposed-actuators` cover the traps above[^cql].
**The strict JAXP template.** Run tests with `java.xml.config.file` pointing to a copy of the JDK's `jaxp-strict.properties.template` to find parsers that fetch DTDs[^jaxp].

**Dependency-Check** needs `failBuildOnCVSS` and an NVD API key[^odc]. Gradle's `--write-verification-metadata sha256` records checksums that fail the build on mismatch[^gradle]. The supply-chain sheet covers the rest.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Oracle JDK 21 updates are no longer free for production.** Releases from 20 October 2026 come under the OTN license; Oracle JDK 25 updates stay free until September 2028[^oracle]. Temurin supports 21 until at least December 2029[^temurin].

**Compromised CA keys need another JDK update.** After eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys were compromised, install a runtime that fixes JDK-8395690 (CVE-2026-114820), even if you updated in October; on Debian and Ubuntu, also rebuild the Java keystore[^ojemudhra].

**Spring Boot 4.0.0 to 4.0.5 could leave every endpoint open** in apps on Boot's default web security with actuator autoconfiguration but without `spring-boot-health` (CVE-2026-40976, critical)[^sp40976].
**Free Spring fixes skip the 3.5 line.** August's critical Spring Security fix (CVE-2026-59270) shipped free only for 7.0 and 7.1[^sp59270].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **The Security Manager.** JDK 24 disabled it for good, and it was rarely used to secure server code[^jep486]. Run untrusted code in its own process or container.
**Hunting gadget classes.** OWASP expects more to be found[^owaspdeser], and Find Security Bugs meant its gadget detector mostly for researchers[^fsb]. Stop deserializing outside data instead.

**Find Security Bugs' inventory patterns.** `SPRING_ENDPOINT` fires on every Spring controller and `SERVLET_PARAMETER` on every request parameter[^fsb]. Exclude them and triage injection findings first.
**CSRF tokens for APIs no browser calls.** Spring says services used only by non-browser clients likely don't need them[^sscsrf].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Exposing actuator, JMX or Jolokia.** `exposure.include=*` publishes every endpoint, and `heapdump`, off by default, returns a heap dump of the running JVM[^actuator]. Serve them only to the monitoring network, behind authentication.
**Turning off CSRF in a browser app.** Spring shows a plain HTML form posting forged JSON as `text/plain`[^sscsrf]. Keep it on wherever session cookies authenticate.

**Updating the host JDK but not the one in the image.** Each standalone runtime has its own `cacerts`, and Debian and Ubuntu need a keystore rebuild[^ojemudhra]. Rebuild images and `jlink` runtimes after every JDK update.

blocks.title: What this looks like for your code

columns.title: New project
items: Start on JDK 25 and Spring Boot 4.1, with `.anyRequest().denyAll()` as the last rule.
Set `-Djdk.serialFilter=!*` and `-Djdk.xml.dtd.support=deny` unless something needs Java serialization or DTDs.
Bind every request to a record and keep entities out of controllers.

columns.title: Existing codebase
items: Move Oracle JDK 21 to JDK 25 or an OpenJDK build, and leave JDK 11 and 17 before October 2027[^temurin].
Search for `ObjectInputStream`, `activateDefaultTyping`, `parseExpression`, `createQuery(` with `+` and `exposure.include`.
Remove Log4j 1, at end of life since 2015[^log4j].

columns.title: High-assurance or regulated
items: Make CodeQL's `security-extended` suite and Find Security Bugs required checks.
Run with an allowlist `jdk.serialFilter` and the strict JAXP template as the JAXP configuration file[^jaxp].
Stay on Spring and JDK lines with free fixes, or pay for support on the ones you keep.
